paths.name: SOC Analyst
paths.summary: The front line of defence. You watch for attacks as they happen, separate real threats from noise and act fast when something is wrong.
day: Escalate real incidents with clear notes
start: Learn how Windows and Linux logs work

paths.name: Digital Forensics & Incident Response
paths.summary: The detective after the break-in. You rebuild exactly what happened, contain the damage and make sure the attacker is really gone.
day: Build timelines from disk, memory and logs
Write up what happened and how to stop it next time

paths.name: Malware Analyst
paths.summary: You take hostile code apart in a safe lab to learn what it does, how it hides and how to detect it everywhere.
day: Run samples in an isolated sandbox
Write YARA rules and share indicators
start: Set up a safe analysis lab
Learn static and dynamic analysis basics
Read assembly with a free disassembler

paths.name: OSINT & Threat Intelligence
paths.summary: You find answers hiding in plain sight. Public data, photos and forums become intelligence that tells defenders who is coming and how.
day: Turn findings into clear intelligence reports
start: Build a toolkit of free OSINT sources

paths.name: Penetration Tester
paths.summary: You break in before the bad guys do. With permission, you attack systems and apps, then explain how to fix every hole you found.
day: Scan and map a target's attack surface
Exploit web, network and Active Directory weaknesses
Write reports developers can act on
start: Get fluent on the Linux command line

paths.name: Governance, Risk & Compliance
paths.summary: You make security work for the whole organisation: the policies, risk decisions and frameworks that stop problems before they start.
day: Map the organisation to frameworks like NIST CSF
Explain security to people outside IT

questions.q: A friend's laptop is acting strange. What's your first instinct?

options.a: Check what's running and when it started
Grab the suspicious file and work out exactly what it does
Figure out how the attacker got in
Make sure there are backups and a plan so it never happens again

questions.q: Which puzzle would you enjoy most?

options.a: Finding where a photo was taken from tiny clues
Breaking into a deliberately vulnerable web app
Spotting the one strange event in thousands of log lines
Taking a program apart to see how it works inside

questions.q: What does your ideal working week look like?

options.a: Fast-paced: lots of quick decisions with a team around me
Deep focus: one hard problem for days
Projects: a new target every few weeks
Research: digging through sources and writing up findings
Structured: frameworks, policies and people across the business

questions.q: Which of these would feel most satisfying?

options.a: Stopping an attack while it's happening
Rebuilding exactly what happened after a breach
Getting a dangerous security hole fixed
Exposing who is behind a scam campaign
Writing a rule that catches a new malware family everywhere

questions.q: How do you feel about writing code?

options.a: I love it
Happy to write small scripts
I'd rather not

questions.q: How about explaining technical things to non-technical people?

options.a: I enjoy it, even presenting to leadership
Fine in small doses
I'd rather let my work speak for itself

questions.q: Which tool would you open first?

options.a: Wireshark, to see what's on the network
A disassembler like Ghidra
A terminal with nmap and Burp Suite
Search engines, maps and social media
A spreadsheet and a risk register

questions.q: It's 2 a.m. and something is on fire. How do you feel?

options.a: Bring it on, I want to be the one who answers the call
I'd rather analyse it calmly in the morning
I'd rather have prevented it in the first place
